posts.title: A delicious "failure" - Medieval bread experiment
posts.description: I decided to try and work with the rye dough and, sadly, only the rye dough. I should have [mixed it with other flours](https://historicalitaliancooking.home.blog/english/recipes/medieval-bread-with-fennel-seeds-and-onion-salad-a-peasants-meal/), which would have been period correct. I did add [fennel seeds](https://www.petersyard.com/recipes/rye-bread/) to it which makes it a good "savory" bread.

posts.title: Wednesday 4 March meal
posts.description: Rice with Raisins This is one of those meals that we'd probably be more likely to eat for breakfast today than just anytime of day during the Renaissance. Overall, it's very simple: Rice cooked in almond milk with a bit of sugar, saffron, and raisins. That's pretty much it. This very basic recipe shows up in a few different places.
